active_paradigms.idea: Exploit an affine gauge and solve the fixed-x maximin subproblem exactly with scipy.optimize.linprog
active_paradigms.description: The current program first finds a configuration by stochastic single-point annealing in a reference triangle, then uses SLSQP on all 26 coordinates with a frozen hull cycle and frozen triangle orientations. Its useful feature is the epigraph formulation, but its main limitation is that a noisy annealing seed and a nonlinear SLSQP solve must simultaneously improve both x and y coordinates. Preserve three outer points at (0,0), (1,0), and (0,1), so the hull area is exactly 1/2 provided every other point remains in this triangle; then the normalized area of a signed triangle is simply its signed determinant. Freeze the x-coordinates and the orientation signs from a strong stored seed, and optimize every non-anchor y-coordinate plus epigraph t in one scipy.optimize.linprog call. With x fixed, every signed determinant is affine in y, so all 286 conditions sign_ijk * determinant_ijk >= t are linear inequalities; simplex membership, y>=0, and x+y<=1 are also linear. This obtains the globally best vertical-coordinate repair for that x-pattern rather than a local nonlinear improvement. Store the resulting configuration as the deterministic return value, or use the LP result directly if its exact recomputed score exceeds the stored seed. This is structurally different from the failed MILP grid approach: it is a continuous exact LP over the actual determinant constraints, not a discretized forbidden-triple proxy.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary min_area_normalized. The fixed triangular affine gauge eliminates the ConvexHull denominator and makes the LP epigraph t exactly equal to the evaluator's normalized minimum area.
active_paradigms.cautions: This requires that exactly the three fixed anchors remain the enclosing hull; explicitly constrain each other point by x>=0, y>=0, x+y<=1. All determinant signs must be taken from a strictly nondegenerate seed and constraints must use the signed determinant, not absolute values. A single LP cannot change the x-pattern or order type, so prepare several offline seeds and deploy only the best validated result; do not perform alternating x/y optimization at runtime.

active_paradigms.idea: Use derivative-free Powell direction-set search on a compact triangular parameterization
active_paradigms.description: The incumbent uses a custom stochastic search followed by gradient-based SLSQP, and freezes its hull topology before polishing. This is effective at avoiding hull discontinuities, but SLSQP can stall because the minimum of 286 absolute determinants is nonsmooth and because many active inequalities have poorly scaled gradients. Use scipy.optimize.fmin_powell as one direct deterministic search call from a hard-coded high-quality configuration, with the three corner anchors held fixed. Parameterize each remaining point by bounded unconstrained variables mapped into the reference triangle, for example x=sigmoid(a) and y=(1-x)*sigmoid(b), so every trial point is valid and the hull denominator remains exactly 1/2. Optimize a robust scalar objective based on the actual minimum signed/absolute determinant, preferably with a small bonus for the mean of the lowest 8 to 16 triangle margins to prevent Powell from exchanging one bottleneck for another nearly equal bottleneck. Powell's line searches can make coordinated long moves along geometric directions that single-point annealing and active-constraint SLSQP often miss, without numerical finite-difference derivatives of a constraint Jacobian. Use a fixed initial direction matrix scaled to the coordinate magnitudes and a fixed iteration/function-evaluation budget, then exact-evaluate the returned array before accepting it. Once found offline, return the numeric array directly to retain near-zero evaluator runtime.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary normalized minimum triangle area, while the low-tail bonus is only a search surrogate intended to leave more than one triangle safely above the final bottleneck and reduce floating-point fragility.
active_paradigms.cautions: Do not optimize the raw ConvexHull result inside the objective: fixing three enclosing corners makes the denominator constant and avoids hull-topology noise. The triangular map must not use clipping, because clipping creates flat line-search regions; use stable bounded transforms and reject non-finite values. The final selected configuration must be scored using all 286 evaluator determinants, since a tail-average surrogate is not itself the metric.

active_paradigms.idea: Use bounded nonlinear least-squares with a smooth all-triangle barrier rather than a guessed square active set
active_paradigms.description: The failed scipy.optimize.root attempt is plausibly brittle because an equioscillation system requires guessing exactly which triangles are active and becomes singular whenever the active set changes. In contrast, scipy.optimize.least_squares can use an overdetermined residual containing all 286 margins, so it does not require a priori active-set correctness. Fix the same three outer anchors to set hull area to 1/2, retain the seed's determinant orientation signs, and optimize the other coordinates and an epigraph variable t within simple coordinate bounds. Construct one smooth residual per triple from a soft hinge such as softplus(beta*(t-signed_det))/beta, which is near zero when that triangle clears t and rises smoothly when it violates t; add a bounded monotone reward residual such as exp(-gamma*t) so the solve pushes t upward while the hinge residuals enforce feasibility. Include only tiny centering or anti-boundary regularization if needed, because the real signal must remain the complete triangle set. A single least_squares call with analytic determinant derivatives or stable numerical scaling can redistribute errors across all near-active triangles more robustly than root's exact equations and can escape the particular SLSQP KKT compromise. Exact postvalidation should keep the result only when its true minimum normalized area exceeds the seed, and the winning coordinates should then be embedded as constants for fast deterministic evaluation.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary min_area_normalized through a smooth feasibility barrier over every evaluator triangle; the method specifically targets the cluster of low-area triangles that limits the incumbent's 0.748167 combined score.
active_paradigms.cautions: The reward/barrier scales beta and gamma are numerical conditioning parameters, not quantities to tune online; choose them offline and make only one solver call in the submitted constructor. Keep t bounded above by a plausible value and use overflow-safe softplus evaluation. Orientation signs and corner containment must remain enforced, otherwise the smooth residual can cross a determinant sign change that invalidates the fixed-order formulation.

tried_paradigms.idea: Deploy an offline-discovered affine-normalized configuration as a constant numpy.array
tried_paradigms.description: The evaluator measures only the returned 13 coordinates and constructor wall time; it does not inspect how those coordinates were found, require a unit-area input region, or reward online optimization. Consequently, use expensive deterministic experimentation outside the submitted constructor to discover the best configuration, evaluate every candidate with exactly the supplied 286-triangle and ConvexHull formulas, and retain the best coordinate table at full double precision. Canonicalize that table by an affine map for numerical stability, for example sending three stable hull vertices to (0,0), (1,0), and (0,1); the normalized score is unchanged by this transformation. The submitted function should then only return a literal 13-by-2 NumPy array, with no random generator, annealing loop, projection, or hull call. This fundamentally separates search cost from evaluation cost and eliminates the current program's weakness that it spends roughly 216,000 stochastic local moves per invocation yet returns whichever local triangular-hull basin happened to win. It also makes exact repeatability automatic and permits use of the free-hull global candidates and local epigraph-polished candidates produced during offline development. Before freezing the table, recompute its score using the exact evaluator code and ensure all near-active determinants have a meaningful numerical margin above zero.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Both the primary normalized area and eval_time: retain the strongest discovered geometry while reducing constructor time to essentially array allocation.
tried_paradigms.cautions: This is only valuable after genuinely finding a superior table; do not round coordinates aggressively because the minimum is controlled by a few nearly equal triangles. Preserve point order and all 13 distinct rows, and verify SciPy ConvexHull sees the intended nondegenerate hull on the target floating-point platform. Do not mistakenly normalize by a presumed triangular area if the stored configuration has a polygonal hull.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace the triangular-hull anneal with one direct global differential-evolution search over unrestricted coordinates
tried_paradigms.description: The current program performs random single-point simulated annealing inside the initial simplex, then applies one SLSQP solve with a frozen hull cycle and frozen determinant signs. Its important strength is that the SLSQP epigraph variable directly represents the normalized minimum oriented triangle area for the selected combinatorial type. Its main limitation is structural: the three initialized corners are always retained, every annealing proposal is projected into their triangle, and the later solver preserves that hull topology, so it effectively searches only triangular-hull arrangements. Use scipy.optimize.differential_evolution directly on all 26 coordinates, with deterministic seed, `workers=1`, `updating='immediate'`, and `polish=False`. The objective should compute the evaluator's exact minimum absolute determinant divided by `ConvexHull(p).volume`, returning a large penalty for degenerate hulls, nonfinite values, or near-zero hull area. Search a bounded square such as [-1,1]^2 for each point; affine and scale invariance mean this bound does not reduce meaningful solution quality. Add only a tiny deterministic tie-breaker based on the mean of the lowest 10 to 20 normalized triangle areas, so broad basins with equal minimum are preferred without changing the primary ranking materially. This lets the optimizer discover four-, five-, or higher-vertex hulls and permits determinant signs and active triangle identities to change, which are exactly the changes the current fixed-topology SLSQP step forbids.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Maximize the exact `min_triangle_area / ConvexHull(points).volume` evaluator value; the secondary low-tail tie-breaker should only stabilize searches and never outweigh the true minimum.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Do not enable DE polishing, because it adds a second optimizer stage and because local polishing on this nonsmooth hull-changing objective is often harmful. Canonically center and scale a candidate only inside objective evaluation if needed for numerical stability, never in a way that changes its score. Catch Qhull failures and assign penalties. Population size and maximum iterations must be chosen for the evaluation timeout, since each objective evaluation computes 286 triangle areas and a convex hull.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use a deterministic grid-packing MILP based on forbidden low-area triples
tried_paradigms.description: Convert a discretized version of the maximin problem into a single exact mixed-integer feasibility/selection problem using scipy.optimize.milp. Construct a deterministic dense candidate set in a fixed unit-area reference triangle or parallelogram, preferably a triangular lattice with several phase offsets encoded in the candidate set. For a chosen raw area threshold t, enumerate every candidate triple whose area is below t and impose the packing inequality `x_i + x_j + x_k <= 2`; no forbidden small triangle can then be selected. Add the cardinality equality `sum_i x_i = 13`, binary integrality, and optionally deterministic symmetry-breaking inequalities on lexicographically equivalent lattice points. If the reference container has area A, every selected hull has area at most A, so a feasible set with every raw triangle area at least t certifies an evaluator score of at least t/A; choose t above the current approximately 0.02315 normalized level rather than optimizing an unrelated surrogate. This attacks the global combinatorial question of which triples can be simultaneously avoided, rather than moving coordinates locally while retaining the incumbent's oriented-matroid type. Return the 13 selected candidate coordinates directly, so the constructor is deterministic and has no annealing variance. The lattice resolution can be increased across submitted program versions, while each version still makes only one MILP call.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly enforce a lower bound on every one of the 286 selected triangle areas, using the fixed container area as a conservative denominator bound; target a threshold whose guaranteed normalized value exceeds 0.02315 and ideally approaches the 0.0309369 benchmark.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The forbidden-triple constraint count can become very large, so generate only triples below the selected threshold and use sparse scipy matrices for `LinearConstraint`. A feasible MILP proves the threshold only on the grid, while infeasibility does not prove continuous infeasibility. Verify the extracted binary solution with the evaluator formula, because solver integrality tolerances can leave values slightly away from 0 or 1. Do not add a coordinate-refinement stage after MILP if adhering to the single-call design.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use deterministic DIRECT search in a low-dimensional threefold-symmetry orbit parameterization
tried_paradigms.description: Exploit the stated geometric prior by parameterizing 13 points as one central point plus four complete 120-degree rotational orbits, giving exactly 1 + 4*3 points. Represent each orbit by a radius and a base angle around a common center, with bounded parameters chosen to prevent numerical coincidence; generate the other two points by fixed rotation matrices. Optimize the exact evaluator ratio of the resulting 13 coordinates using scipy.optimize.direct, which is deterministic bounded global partitioning rather than random annealing or local SLSQP. DIRECT is particularly appropriate here because the orbit parameterization reduces the dimensionality from 26 to roughly 8 to 10 variables and no hull ordering, determinant sign pattern, or active constraint set has to be assumed. Its objective should again use the true minimum over all 286 absolute areas and actual convex-hull area, with robust penalties for degenerate configurations. The current code's useful observation is that many near-minimal triangles should be jointly balanced; this symmetry parameterization creates such equality patterns automatically instead of relying on a weak low-tail annealing reward. Allow the common center to be a two-dimensional parameter rather than forcing it to the origin, although translation does not affect the score, because this makes coordinate bounds easier to manage. The best symmetric family may have a nontriangular hull, unlike the current construction, and DIRECT can change the number of exposed orbit points without a topology constraint.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Search for a high-quality balanced configuration with many equal or nearly equal critical triangle areas, maximizing the exact normalized minimum while reducing the global search dimension enough to make deterministic exploration practical.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Threefold symmetry is a powerful structural hypothesis, not a theorem for n=13; it can miss an asymmetric optimum, so it should be evaluated as an independent candidate family rather than imposed on every search. Keep radii away from zero for orbit points, since a collapsed orbit creates duplicate points and zero-area triangles. DIRECT becomes expensive as dimensions and `maxfun` rise, so use a compact orbit parameterization and set an explicit function-evaluation budget. Handle ConvexHull exceptions inside the objective because some radial-angle combinations are nearly collinear.

tried_paradigms.idea: Offline global order-type discovery with scipy.optimize.dual_annealing in an affine gauge
tried_paradigms.description: The current program first performs a hand-written random-walk anneal in a fixed unit triangle and then uses SLSQP only within the discovered hull cycle and determinant-sign cell. Its strength is that the fixed three corners remove scale freedom and make the subsequent epigraph constraints meaningful, but its main limitation is that the annealing schedule explores only a small and noisy subset of possible order types before SLSQP permanently locks one of them. Replace the custom annealing discovery phase with a single offline scipy.optimize.dual_annealing call on the 20 coordinates of the ten non-anchor points, keeping anchors at (0,0), (1,0), and (0,1). Parameterize or penalize every free point outside x>=0, y>=0, x+y<=1, so the hull area is exactly 1/2 and the objective is simply the smallest absolute determinant divided by one. Use the exact evaluator minimum rather than the current minimum-plus-mean surrogate, because the surrogate can sacrifice the actual bottleneck in exchange for improving the next eleven triangles. Run this expensive call offline with a fixed seed, high visit parameter, and enough iterations to discover a superior order type, then embed only its resulting 13 coordinates in the submitted constructor as a constant array. This produces deterministic near-zero evaluation time while retaining the global-search benefit during construction discovery.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary min_area_normalized; fixing the reference triangle makes convex-hull area constant, eliminates affine redundancy, and permits direct optimization of the evaluator bottleneck. The deployed constant also minimizes eval_time.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Use no local-search callback or second polishing stage if enforcing the single-call rule. Reject or heavily penalize configurations with a determinant below a numerical tolerance, and independently recompute all 286 areas and ConvexHull area before freezing coordinates. Do not normalize coordinates pointwise after optimization, since that changes triangle relations; only use a globally affine-equivalent representation.

tried_paradigms.idea: Solve an equioscillation active-set system using scipy.optimize.root
tried_paradigms.description: At a local maximin arrangement, several distinct triangles should be simultaneously tight; improvement normally requires moving the entire active contact set together rather than moving one point at a time. The current SLSQP polish is vulnerable to its inherited signs, hull topology, and feasibility tolerances, and it may stop with a cluster of almost-tight triangles that are not exactly equal. Starting from an offline stored candidate, identify the smallest-area triangles and select a full-rank set of independent active determinant equations after affine-gauging three hull vertices. Form a nonlinear residual system whose equations set every selected signed triangle determinant equal to 2t, with t included as an unknown; add deterministic gauge equations and, when needed, stationarity/equalization equations derived from the active set so the system is square. Call scipy.optimize.root once from that stored candidate to solve this geometric contact system at high precision. Evaluate the returned point set exactly over all 286 triangles, retaining it only if its true normalized score exceeds the seed and the intended anchor triangle remains the hull. This is fundamentally a geometric certificate-refinement method rather than another stochastic search or constrained epigraph solve, and is especially useful once a promising combinatorial type has been found.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Numerical sharpening of the limiting triangle areas and removal of small slack disparities that reduce min_area_normalized. It can improve a fixed order type without runtime exploration.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The active triangles must have a full-rank Jacobian; blindly including all near-active constraints makes the root system singular. Preserve each selected triangle orientation through a fixed sign, and validate the actual convex hull afterward because root has no inequality enforcement. Use this as an offline one-call refinement and embed the validated result, not as an unbounded runtime recovery mechanism.

tried_paradigms.description: Exploit the stated geometric prior directly instead of asking a 26-variable stochastic search to rediscover symmetry. Represent 13 points as one center point plus four rotational orbits of three points under exact 120-degree rotation, so only four representative planar positions are free after fixing the center at the rotational origin. Build all 13 coordinates analytically from those representatives, evaluate the same all-286-triangle minimum divided by the actual hull area, and use scipy.optimize.shgo over bounded polar or Cartesian representative parameters. The greatly reduced dimension lets SHGO systematically partition the domain and compare many basins that the current 12 annealing restarts may never enter. Constrain one outer orbit to define a nondegenerate enclosing triangle or impose a positive hull-area guard, while allowing the remaining orbits to move freely; affine normalization can be applied once to the final configuration. If the best symmetric result exceeds the current 0.748167 relative score, deploy its coordinates directly; even if it does not, its active-triangle pattern is a strong seed/order-type hypothesis for an asymmetric offline construction. Exact rotational generation also gives platform-independent reproducibility without depending on fragile random acceptance histories.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Global structural quality of min_area_normalized through exact 3-fold symmetry, reduced search dimension, and systematic basin coverage; deployment as constants gives negligible eval_time.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Symmetry is a hypothesis, not a theorem for n=13, so compare its exact evaluator score against an unrestricted candidate rather than assuming it is optimal. Avoid representatives with equal radii and aligned angles that create orbit-induced collinear triples. SHGO should be the sole search call, with finite bounds and a large penalty for nearly zero hull area or duplicate points.

tried_paradigms.idea: Solve a fixed oriented-matroid contact system with scipy.optimize.least_squares
tried_paradigms.description: The current program first uses stochastic single-point annealing inside a fixed reference triangle, then SLSQP maximizes an epigraph margin while freezing the discovered hull cycle and signs of all 286 determinants. Its strength is that the epigraph formulation correctly targets the evaluator ratio and its sign/hull constraints prevent the nonsmooth absolute-value objective from changing combinatorial type. Its main weakness is that the annealer must discover both the oriented matroid and which triangle constraints are active, while SLSQP only improves the one topology it happens to find; its 12 × 18,000-loop search is also expensive at evaluation time. Instead, take a high-quality known configuration and identify a stable active set consisting of all triangles within, for example, 1–3% of the minimum normalized area, plus hull-support constraints. Parameterize a fixed affine gauge, such as three hull vertices at (0,0), (1,0), (0,1), so that hull area is constant and the target is simply a determinant margin. Call scipy.optimize.least_squares once on residuals that enforce equal determinant values for the active triangles, enforce zero first-order force/KKT balance through nonnegative active-triangle multipliers, and include soft positive-margin residuals for every inactive triangle. This attacks the likely equioscillation structure of a true local maximin optimum rather than maximizing only an epigraph variable through a generic constrained optimizer. Verify the returned point set using all 286 exact areas and retain a precomputed fallback array if the candidate changes hull topology or loses margin.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Increase min_area_normalized by solving the equal-area contact geometry more accurately; eliminate repeated annealing/SLSQP runtime so eval_time is also much lower.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The determinant signs and hull order must be taken from a validated seed and held fixed during the solve. Do not use only the currently smallest three triangles: include a sufficiently broad near-active set or the solution will overfit and create a new smaller inactive triangle. Gauge away affine degrees of freedom, scale residuals comparably, and return a fixed stored fallback if least_squares does not converge or exact evaluator recomputation is worse.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use a one-shot linear-program slice search with scipy.optimize.linprog
tried_paradigms.description: Exploit the fact that, once all x-coordinates and the orientation signs are fixed, every signed triangle determinant is affine in the y-coordinates. Fix an affine gauge and a candidate hull topology, fix the x-coordinate ordering from a good seed or from a deliberately designed interleaving pattern, and use scipy.optimize.linprog with variables y_1,...,y_13 and margin t. Add one inequality per oriented triple requiring signed_det(x,y) >= 2t, and add linear inequalities placing all non-hull points to the interior side of each directed hull edge; if the outer hull is fixed as a triangle, its area is constant and this directly maximizes the evaluator numerator. Bounds on y and explicit separation/order inequalities make the LP numerically stable and preserve the intended oriented matroid. This is fundamentally different from the failed grid MILP: it does not discretize point locations or approximate areas, but optimizes a continuous exact determinant slice globally. It also differs from the current SLSQP because for a fixed x slice it obtains the globally optimal y/margin rather than a local nonlinear answer. Offline, compare a small catalog of manually selected x-order patterns derived from the current seed and permanently embed the best resulting coordinates, so the submitted constructor need only return the selected array.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly maximize the exact minimum signed triangle area in a continuous convex subproblem, seeking a better combinatorial realization while retaining negligible runtime in the final returned constant.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The LP is only valid while x values, determinant orientations, and hull-edge directions remain fixed; do not allow a solution whose presumed hull edges become nonconvex. If hull area is not explicitly fixed by affine gauge, the ratio becomes fractional/nonlinear and linprog no longer represents the evaluator objective. Strict inequalities need a small positive buffer, and exact post-checking over all 286 absolute areas is mandatory before accepting an offline result.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.root to enforce an active-set KKT equilibrium rather than re-running random annealing
tried_paradigms.description: The present annealing stage makes local random moves scored by the smallest dozen areas, which helps avoid optimizing a single accidental bottleneck, but it has no mechanism for recognizing or satisfying the stationarity equations of the final maximin arrangement. At a genuine locally optimal fixed-topology solution, several triangle-area constraints should tie at the common margin and their signed gradients should admit a balancing combination that cancels in every free point coordinate after affine gauge fixing. Extract an active contact graph from the best existing configuration: include the tight triangles and enough nearly tight alternatives to make the number of independent equations comparable to the free coordinate count. Define scipy.optimize.root residuals from equalities between active normalized determinants, the KKT gradient-balance equations with multiplier variables, multiplier normalization, and fixed affine gauge equations. A single root solve can move directly to a sharp nonsmooth vertex that SLSQP often approaches only approximately because its active set and multipliers are unstable around tied constraints. Use deterministic initial coordinates and positive initial multipliers from a nonnegative least-squares fit, then accept only a root whose full 286-triangle score improves the stored seed. The deployment result should again be baked into a constant array, making the evaluator deterministic and avoiding the current substantial random-search cost.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Improve the primary normalized minimum area by resolving the active-constraint equilibrium to high precision; improve eval_time by replacing online annealing with an offline-discovered deterministic configuration.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Root solving is not a global search and is only useful after selecting a credible active set from a strong seed. The active set can be rank-deficient because of affine invariance, so explicitly fix six affine degrees of freedom or use a square independent equation subset. Reject roots with negative multipliers, changed determinant signs, changed hull cycle, or any newly violated inactive triangle; retain the known configuration on every failure path.
